title: Welcome to midterm silly season 🤡
contentHtml:
New FLIPR landing pages for our Senate, House and governor forecasts

To make navigation easier, we’ve moved FLIPR’s House, Senate, and gubernatorial forecasts to separate landing pages. The original FLIPR homepage is still in the same place, though, and contains complete polling averages, our topline forecast, and other “best of” charts along with links to everything else.

Still Counting Episode 6 is ready. Here’s the video:

And here’s the audio. (Once again, we’re very grateful for your reviews, comments, likes and subscribes.) With just 19 days to go until the midterms, it was a lively episode, as Galen, Clare and I played a round of “Do You Buy It?” for various storylines that range from serious to kind of insane — sorry, but I’m not sure how else to describe the Talarico thing.

The context

The first election I covered in 2008 spoiled me. That campaign was dynamic pretty much from start to finish. After Barack Obama’s historic nomination following an epic primary battle against Hillary Clinton, John McCain surged in the polls after his surprising choice of Sarah Palin as his running mate. That pick didn’t age well, of course. But McCain’s bigger problem was that the financial system was at its most vulnerable point since the 1930s after Lehman Brothers
